simple.meaning: בָּרָה (bârâh) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to select ; to feed ; to render clear.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 7 times in 1 Samuel, 2 Samuel, Lamentations, beginning at 1 Samuel 17:8. The surrounding contexts include family, kingship, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to בָּרָה (H1262) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: בָּרָה (bârâh) / H1262 is traced through 1 Samuel 17:8, 2 Samuel 3:35, 2 Samuel 12:17, 2 Samuel 13:5 with source-language evidence and verse context.

firstOccurrence.englishText: He stood and cried to the armies of Israel, and said to them, “Why have you come out to set your battle in array? Am I not a Philistine, and you servants to Saul? Choose a man for yourselves, and let him come down to me.

timeline.evidenceText: He stood and cried to the armies of Israel, and said to them, “Why have you come out to set your battle in array? Am I not a Philistine, and you servants to Saul? Choose a man for yourselves, and let him come down to me.
All the people came to urge David to eat bread while it was yet day; but David swore, saying, “God do so to me, and more also, if I taste bread, or anything else, until the sun goes down.”
The elders of his house arose beside him, to raise him up from the earth: but he would not, and he didn’t eat bread with them.

Jonadab said to him, “Lay down on your bed, and pretend to be sick. When your father comes to see you, tell him, ‘Please let my sister Tamar come and give me bread to eat, and prepare the food in my sight, that I may see it, and eat it from her hand.’ ”

So Amnon lay down and faked being sick. When the king came to see him, Amnon said to the king, “Please let my sister Tamar come, and make me a couple of cakes in my sight, that I may eat from her hand.”
Amnon said to Tamar, “Bring the food into the room, that I may eat from your hand.” Tamar took the cakes which she had made, and brought them into the room to Amnon her brother.
The hands of the pitiful women have boiled their own children.

definitions.short: to select ; to feed ; to render clear
definitions.full: H1262. barah I. בָּרָה verb eat (Assyrian barû & derivatives Zim BP 31 ) — Qal Perfect 2Sam 12:17 ; Imperfect אֶבְרֶה 13:6 , 10 eat bread ( בְּרוּלְֿכֶם 1Sam 17:8 scribal error for לכם בחרו 1Kin 18:25 Dr Sm 107 ). Pi`el Infinitive לְבָרוֺת Lam 4:10 for devouring . Hiph`il Imperfect תַּבְרֵנִי 2Sam 13:5 ; Infinitive לְהַבְרוֺת 3:35 cause to eat bread .
definitions.rootNote: a primitive root; to select; also (as denominative from 1250 ) to feed; also (as equivalent to 1305 ) to render clear (Ecclesiastes 3:18)
